reasons: Directionally correct: we act for the Customer, and the Company (Deerskin) is our party under the hosting agreement, so extending the Section 1.4 access/use rights to our Affiliates and contractors is a benefit-side edit, not a concession.

Deviation classification is supportable: Section 1.4 grants access and use to "the Company" alone, with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no written-notice mechanic, which fails the fallback's material term (affiliates covered at least on written notice); Section 10.3's "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" makes the silence exclusionary rather than neutral, so it is not an acceptable fallback clause that would make this over-flagging.

Redline is actionable and reads cleanly when merged with p0008 ("HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and the right for the Company, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf to use, a computer system..."), and the Section 10.3 insertion preserves the original no-third-party-rights language while carving out Affiliates/contractors and adding the successor transfer per the rule's redline guidance.
Failed minimal-edit heuristic on p0063 (0.827) is explained by the length of the inserted proviso; the surviving original wording is intact, so this is not an unnecessary rewrite.

Minor gaps noted, not disqualifying: the redline uses capitalised "Affiliates" although no Affiliate definition appears in the resolved definitions — add a short definition (or lower-case "affiliates") to avoid an undefined term; the "access to" limb of 1.4 still names only the Company, so the extension rests on the "right to use" limb.

Rationale slightly overstates by framing the standard no-third-party-rights sentence as the rule's walk-away trigger; the finding stands on the failed fallback element regardless, and Section 10.3 contains no anti-assignment prohibition, so the successor-transfer element was only weakly at risk.
